rounds.text: Eyantra Ventures Ltd is positioned inside a broader services sector that enjoys a clear macroeconomic tailwind with a score of +0.59 [E57, E58], alongside healthy sector-wide median sales growth of 11.8% [E60]. The company is actively capturing this commercial environment, demonstrated by a robust compounded sales growth rate of 103% over the trailing twelve months [E13]. Operational efficiency is also improving concurrently, as evidenced by a substantial compression in working capital requirements from 65.3 days down to 37.3 days [E45]. Furthermore, filed statements explicitly flag that the company is expected to deliver a good quarter [E44]. Balance sheet liquidity remains highly comfortable, underlined by a current ratio of 8.73x recorded in March 2025 [E28]. Finally, the stock trades directly near its 52-week low [E52], sitting at just 2% of the way up its yearly range [E4] and -46.0% away from its high [E34], offering an entry point after a 43.1% twelve-month pullback [E37]. Conceded: [E14], [E21], [E24].

Eyantra Ventures Ltd carries fundamental operational and valuation risks that are entirely unsupported by its current pricing multiples. The company exhibits a severely negative return profile, highlighted by an ROE of -16.4% and an ROCE of -8.4%, drastically underperforming sector benchmarks where sector median ROCE stands at 7.4% [E8, E11, E61]. Compounded profit growth has collapsed by -166% alongside a deteriorating operating margin that sits at 0% in TTM and worsened further to -12% in the June 2026 quarter [E13, E14, E19, E20]. Cash generation is deeply troubled, with operating cash flow plunging to -11.57 Cr and free cash flow dropping to -17.27 Cr in March 2026, while borrowings spiked heavily from 0.86 Cr to 16.46 Cr over the same period [E24, E25, E29]. Market valuation remains disconnected from these poor fundamentals, trading at an exorbitant EV/EBITDA of 180.31x against a sector benchmark of 12.08x, a P/B of 3.87x versus a sector median of 1.51x, and a low rules-based screen score of 22 out of 100 [E6, E10, E51]. Furthermore, technical momentum is exceptionally weak with the stock sitting right at its 52-week low, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and suffering a promoter holding reduction down to 62.29% [E31, E33, E35]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reached 103% and the services sector maintains a positive tailwind score of 0.59 [E13, E57].

Conceded: ROE is -16.4%, ROCE is -8.4%, profit growth is -166%, operating cash flow is -11.57 Cr, free cash flow is -17.27 Cr, borrowings rose to 16.46 Cr, EV/EBITDA is 180.31x, P/B is 3.87x, the screen score is 22/100, the stock is at its 52-week low below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and promoter holding is 62.29% [E6, E8, E10, E11, E14, E24, E25, E29, E31, E33, E35, E51]. However, the business is capturing tremendous top-line demand with compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reaching an impressive 103% [E13]. This massive revenue acceleration is operating directly within a supportive macro backdrop, as the services sector enjoys a robust tailwind score of 0.59 [E57]. Furthermore, working capital efficiency has substantially improved, with requirements dropping dramatically from 65.3 days down to 37.3 days [E45]. Management is also actively positioning the enterprise operationally for upcoming periods, being explicitly expected to deliver a good quarter [E44].

Conceded: compounded sales growth reached 103% TTM, the services sector has a tailwind score of 0.59, working capital requirements dropped to 37.3 days, and management is expected to deliver a good quarter [E13, E44, E45, E57]. However, this top-line surge has failed to translate into actual earnings or cash generation, as evidenced by a compounded profit growth of -166% alongside a negative operating cash flow of Rs -11.57 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -17.27 Cr [E14, E24, E25]. The lower working capital requirement has not prevented debtors from worsening as debtor days actually increased from 90.3 to 108 days [E49]. Furthermore, borrowing has spiked from Rs 0.86 Cr to Rs 16.46 Cr while profitability metrics remain heavily distressed with an ROE of -16.4% and an interest coverage ratio flagged as low [E8, E29, E47]. Expectations of a good quarter do not justify paying a stretched P/B of 3.87x and an astronomical EV/EBITDA of 180.31x for a loss-making enterprise whose promoters continue to reduce their stake [E6, E10, E31].
